question: Should OpenClaw adopt the experiment-gated `claws update --dry-run` workflow and `openclaw.clawUpdatePlan.v1` schema as the core consent contract for grouped Claw updates?
rationale: Tests can establish planner behavior, but they cannot decide whether this new core CLI and versioned compatibility surface belongs in the product or how strongly an experimental contract should constrain later revisions.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded planner
options.body: Approve the read-only planner as the RFC’s consent boundary, then land it after its prerequisite and required checks are green.

options.title: Narrow the contract first
options.body: Keep the planning implementation but reduce or explicitly qualify the externally stable schema surface before merging the stack.

options.title: Defer the Claws stack
options.body: Pause or close the implementation slices until maintainers accept a different RFC or product direction.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded planner
recommendation.body: Approve the read-only planner as the RFC’s consent boundary, then land it after its prerequisite and required checks are green.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the assigned reviewer and have already performed the deepest maintainer-facing contract review available in the item history.
